chunks: Abi (peace be upon him) from Sa’d ibn Abdillah from al-Fadl ibn ‘Amir from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Haytham ibn Waqid who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Whatever blessing Allah bestows upon a servant that reaches its fullness, if he praises Allah for it, his praise of Allah is superior to that blessing, greater and heavier.

key_terms.أَوْزَنَ: heavier in weight (in the scale of deeds)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praising Allah for His blessings?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-Amal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the metaphysical weight of gratitude, where the act of thanksgiving is not merely a response but a superior spiritual reality. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *shukr* as a transformative state that elevates the soul beyond the mere possession of the blessing, aligning with the concept that the receiver's acknowledgment amplifies the giver's glory. It serves as a practical reminder for believers to cultivate constant awareness of divine favors to maximize their spiritual reward.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. Abi (rah) from Sa’d b. Abdillah from al-Fadhl b. ’Amir from Musa b. al-Qasim from Safwan b. Yahya from al-Haytham b. Waqid who said I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
If Allah has given His slave great bounties then if he praises Allah for those bounties this praise is better and heavier than that bounty.”
